A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same research work, including VASE, VALEE, Table 1, and complete Appendices A–C. Text extraction and rendered-page inspection support reliable comparison of the algorithms, equations, proofs, and presentation.

before.justification: v1 reports algorithms, theoretical regret bounds, and proofs. Table 1 summarizes theoretical rates; neither the main text nor the appendices contains original empirical results.

after.justification: v2 likewise contains theoretical analysis and proofs, without original experiments, simulations, user studies, or data-analysis outcomes in the main text or appendices.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 removes the explicit loop over i in [d] around the SR variance estimate for a fixed action, leaving one SR call. This is a local procedural correction; the overall VASE and VALEE strategies remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Neither version uses datasets or conducts empirical evaluations. The theoretical coverage of finite action sets and ℓp unit balls is retained; Bayesian bandits are added only as related-work context.

E2.justification: Neither version evaluates comparison algorithms experimentally. The newly cited Bayesian-bandit works supply background theoretical bounds, rather than additional evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Neither version contains empirical evaluation protocols, data splits, training budgets, or benchmark testing procedures. No such settings are introduced or revised.

E4.justification: Neither version contains ablations, robustness experiments, sensitivity studies, or empirical case studies. Appendices A–C retain their mathematical analyses and proofs.

E5.justification: Neither reports experimental seeds, repeated-run counts, error bars, or significance tests. The confidence parameters in the theoretical guarantees remain unchanged.

E6.justification: Table 1 and the principal regret theorems retain the same results. No empirical scores, rankings, or experimental outcome entries are added, removed, or revised.

T1.justification: Section 3.2.1 corrects the stated ℓ2 estimation error from ε tr(Σ) to ε√tr(Σ), aligning its mathematical dependence with the already-correct Lemma 3.11. The main theorem statements and appendix derivations remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statements, and discussion retain the same claims about variance-dependent regret, the VASE and VALEE algorithms, matching lower bounds under the stated conditions, and known versus unknown covariance.

C2.justification: The geometric and variance-based explanations remain unchanged. Both versions retain the unknown-covariance regret gap and the open question of matching the σq²-dependent lower bound for p > 2. The added Impact Statement supplies no substantive limitation.

D1.justification: Algorithms 2–3 specify previously omitted sampling-time initialization and updates, including t1, tℓ, tj, tj,ℓ, and the update tj ← tj + κTj(exp). These additions make the pseudocode's bookkeeping more explicit.

R1.justification: Section 1.1 adds a Bayesian Linear Bandits paragraph and references to Russo and Van Roy (2014) and Dani et al. (2007), relating Bayesian-risk rates to additive-noise bounds. The existing positioning against adversarial and variance-dependent approaches is retained.

P1.justification: v2 makes limited introductory and grammatical edits, adds Bayesian related work and a generic Impact Statement, and replaces the preprint footer with conference-proceedings text. The main section and appendix organization remains intact.

P2.justification: Algorithm 1 moves from page 4 to page 5, Algorithms 2–3 switch columns, and the text and bibliography reflow. Table 1 is unchanged. A long reference URL previously clipped at the page edge now overlaps the neighboring bibliography column on v2 page 10.

improvement.justification: Removing Algorithm 1's redundant loop, specifying sampling-time bookkeeping, and correcting the error expression improve consistency and implementability without changing the main guarantees or proofs. There are localized drawbacks: the new Bayesian paragraph does not justify its entropy bound for the stated parameter prior, and a reference URL overlaps another column. These limit, but do not outweigh, the modest gains from the corrections.
